name: Felbamate
summary: Felbamate is a seizure medicine kept for severe epilepsy that hasn't responded to other treatments, because it carries a rare but serious risk of aplastic anemia and liver failure.
description: Felbamate is a seizure medicine that blocks NMDA receptors and changes how GABA-A receptors respond. Because it can cause rare but serious side effects, such as aplastic anemia (the bone marrow stops making blood cells) and liver failure, felbamate is used only for severe epilepsy that hasn't responded to other treatments, including Lennox–Gastaut syndrome and partial seizures that other medicines haven't controlled.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content: Felbamate is an anticonvulsant that inhibits NMDA receptor activity and modulates GABA-A receptor responses. Due to its association with rare but serious adverse effects, such as aplastic anemia and hepatic failure, felbamate is reserved for severe, treatment-resistant epilepsy, including Lennox–Gastaut syndrome and refractory partial seizures.
